cim: The New York Times Opinion Hires Jasmine Sun to Cover Artificial Intelligence and Technology
cim_eredeti: The New York Times Opinion Hires Jasmine Sun to Cover Artificial Intelligence and Technology
szoveg_eredeti:
The New York Times has appointed Jasmine Sun to its Opinion section, where she will cover artificial intelligence and technology, bringing experience in Silicon Valley, product management and technology journalism to the publication.

In her new role, Sun will lead a weekly newsletter focused on artificial intelligence, contribute to the development of editorials addressing technology and related issues, and participate in the publication’s expanding audio and video programming.

She will also appear as an occasional guest on the relaunched Hard Fork podcast and contribute to Opinion Shows, extending her coverage across multiple editorial formats.

Sun brings a combination of technology industry experience and independent publishing expertise to The New York Times.

Before joining the publication, she worked as a product manager at Substack, the digital publishing platform that enables writers and creators to distribute newsletters and subscription-based content.

During her tenure at Substack, Sun helped develop strategies supporting the platform’s growth, gaining firsthand experience with digital publishing, audience development and the technology industry’s business models.

She also co-founded Reboot, a publication focused on young technologists and their perspectives on technology, culture and the industry’s broader influence.

Through Reboot, Sun contributed to discussions about the technology sector and the experiences of emerging professionals working within it.

Her editorial experience also includes helping research and edit The A.G.I. Chronicles, the latest book by Kevin Roose, a technology journalist at The New York Times.

The project further developed her experience examining artificial intelligence and its implications for technology and society.

Sun’s appointment comes as artificial intelligence continues to reshape the technology industry, creating demand for reporting and commentary that examines the development, commercialization and broader consequences of emerging AI systems.

Her background combines direct experience working inside a technology company with independent editorial work, providing perspectives on both the business and cultural dimensions of technological change.

At The New York Times Opinion, Sun will focus on artificial intelligence while contributing to broader editorial discussions about technology.

Her weekly newsletter will provide a dedicated outlet for her analysis, while her involvement in Hard Fork and Opinion Shows will expand her presence across the publication’s multimedia offerings.

Sun is a graduate of Stanford University and is based in San Francisco, placing her near the center of the Silicon Valley technology industry.

Her appointment adds a technology-focused writer to The New York Times Opinion team as the publication expands its coverage and commentary on artificial intelligence and the rapidly evolving technology sector.
